sentences.zh: 昔八卦兆而天人之理著，九疇序而帝王之應明。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Eight Trigrams appeared and the principle of Heaven and man was made manifest; the Nine Categories were ordered and the responses of emperors and kings were clarified.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Eight Trigrams appeared and the principle of Heaven and man was made manifest; the Nine Categories were ordered and the responses of emperors and kings were clarified.

sentences.zh: 雖可以知從德獲自天之祐，違道陷神聽之罪，然未詳舉徵效，備考幽明，雖時列鼎雉庭穀之異，然而未究者眾矣。

translations.literal: Although one may know that following virtue wins Heaven's blessing and violating the Way falls into the crime of divine hearing, yet omens and effects have not been fully set forth, and a complete examination of the hidden and manifest remains wanting — though the times list such anomalies as tripods, pheasants, and courtyard grain, still what has not been investigated is numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Although one may know that following virtue wins Heaven's blessing and violating the Way falls into the crime of divine hearing, the omens and effects have not been fully set forth and a complete examination of the hidden and manifest remains wanting — though the times list such anomalies as tripods, pheasants, and courtyard grain, what has not been investigated remains numerous.

sentences.zh: 至於鑑悟後王，多有所闕。

translations.literal: As for illuminating and awakening later kings, much is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: As for illuminating and awakening later kings, much remains lacking.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼作春秋，具書祥眚，以驗行事。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, fully recording auspices and calamities to verify conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, fully recording auspices and calamities to verify conduct.

sentences.zh: 是則九疇陳其義於前，春秋列其效於後也。

translations.literal: Thus the Nine Categories set forth their meaning beforehand, and the Spring and Autumn Annals listed their effects afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Nine Categories set forth their meaning beforehand, and the Spring and Autumn Annals listed their effects afterward.

sentences.zh: 逮至伏生創紀大傳，五行之體始詳；

translations.literal: When it reached Fu Sheng's creation of the Great Commentary, the substance of the Five Elements first became detailed;
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Sheng composed the Great Commentary, the substance of the Five Elements first became detailed;

sentences.zh: 劉向廣演洪範，休咎之文益備。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang broadly expounded the Great Plan, and the texts on blessing and calamity became more complete.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang broadly expounded the Great Plan, and the texts on blessing and calamity became more complete.

sentences.zh: 故班固斟酌經、傳，詳紀條流，誠以一王之典，不可獨闕故也。

translations.literal: Therefore Ban Gu weighed the classics and commentaries and recorded in detail each category and branch — truly because the statutes of a single dynasty cannot be allowed to stand alone incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Ban Gu weighed the classics and commentaries and recorded each category and branch in detail — truly because the statutes of a single dynasty cannot be allowed to stand alone incomplete.

sentences.zh: 夫天道雖無聲無臭，然而應若影響，天人之驗，理不可誣。

translations.literal: Now the Way of Heaven, though without sound and without odor, yet responds like shadow and echo; the verification of Heaven and man — its principle cannot be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of Heaven, though without sound and without odor, responds like shadow and echo; the verification of Heaven and man — its principle cannot be deceived.

sentences.zh: 司馬彪纂集光武以來，以究漢事；

translations.literal: Sima Biao compiled and gathered from Guangwu onward to investigate Han affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao compiled and gathered from Guangwu onward to investigate Han affairs;

sentences.zh: 王沈魏書志篇闕，凡厥災異，但編帝紀而已。

translations.literal: Wang Shen's Book of Wei lacked treatise chapters; all such disasters and anomalies were only compiled in the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen's Book of Wei lacked treatise chapters; all such disasters and anomalies were only compiled in the imperial annals.

sentences.zh: 自黃初以降，二百餘年，覽其災妖，以考之事，常若重規沓矩，不謬前說。

translations.literal: From Huangchu downward, over two hundred years, surveying its disasters and prodigies and examining them against events, they constantly accord like overlapping compasses and stacked carpenter's squares, not contradicting prior explanations.
translations.idiomatic: From Huangchu downward, over two hundred years, surveying its disasters and prodigies and examining them against events, they constantly accord like overlapping compasses and stacked carpenter's squares, not contradicting prior explanations.

sentences.zh: 又高堂隆、郭景純等，據經立辭，終皆顯應。

translations.literal: Further, Gaotang Long, Guo Jingchun, and others, grounding their words in the classics, in the end all found clear fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Further, Gaotang Long, Guo Jingchun, and others, grounding their words in the classics, in the end all found clear fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 闕而不序，史體將虧。

translations.literal: To leave them out without ordering them — the form of history would be damaged.
translations.idiomatic: To leave them out without ordering them — the form of history would be damaged.

sentences.zh: 今自司馬彪以後，皆撰次論序，斯亦班固遠采春秋，舉遠明近之例也。

translations.literal: Now from Sima Biao onward, all have been composed and arranged with discussion and prefaces — this too is Ban Gu's example of drawing remotely from the Spring and Autumn Annals to illuminate the near.
translations.idiomatic: Now from Sima Biao onward, all have been composed and arranged with discussion and prefaces — this too is Ban Gu's example of drawing remotely from the Spring and Autumn Annals to illuminate the near.

sentences.zh: 又按言之不從，有介蟲之孽，劉歆以為毛蟲；

translations.literal: Again, when speech is not followed, there is the calamity of shell-bearing creatures; Liu Xin took them to be hairy creatures;
translations.idiomatic: Again, when speech is not followed, there is the calamity of shell-bearing creatures; Liu Xin took them to be hairy creatures;

sentences.zh: 視之不明，有蠃蟲之孽，劉歆以為羽蟲。

translations.literal: when vision is not clear, there is the calamity of naked creatures; Liu Xin took them to be feathered creatures.
translations.idiomatic: when vision is not clear, there is the calamity of naked creatures; Liu Xin took them to be feathered creatures.

sentences.zh: 按月令，夏蟲羽，秋蟲毛，宜如歆說，是以舊史從之。

translations.literal: According to the Monthly Ordinances, summer creatures are feathered and autumn creatures are hairy — Liu Xin's explanation is appropriate, and therefore the earlier histories followed it.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Monthly Ordinances, summer creatures are feathered and autumn creatures are hairy — Liu Xin's explanation is appropriate, and therefore the earlier histories followed it.

sentences.zh: 五行精微，非末學所究。

translations.literal: The subtleties of the Five Elements are not what shallow learning can exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: The subtleties of the Five Elements are not what shallow learning can exhaust.

sentences.zh: 凡已經前議者，並即其言以釋之；

translations.literal: For all that have already been discussed by earlier commentators, I take their words to explain them;
translations.idiomatic: For all that have already been discussed by earlier commentators, I take their words to explain them;

sentences.zh: 未有舊說者，推準事理，以俟來哲。

translations.literal: where no prior explanation exists, I infer by analogy from principle and fact, awaiting later sages.
translations.idiomatic: where no prior explanation exists, I infer by analogy from principle and fact, awaiting later sages.

sentences.zh: 五行傳曰：「田獵不宿，飲食不享，出入不節，奪民農時，及有姦謀，則木不曲直，謂木失其性而為災也。

translations.literal: The Five Elements Commentary says: "If hunting does not lodge overnight, eating and drinking are not offered in sacrifice, coming and going lack restraint, the people's farming seasons are seized, and there are treacherous plots — then wood loses its bending and straightening; this means wood has lost its nature and become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Elements Commentary says: "When hunts roll on without pause, feasts ignore sacrificial propriety, movement ignores measure, corvées steal the farming calendar, and treachery festers — then wood forfeits its office of bending and straightening; this means wood has lost its nature and become a disaster.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅。

translations.literal: " It also says: "When bearing lacks respect, this is called lacking solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "When bearing lacks respect, this is called lacking solemnity.

sentences.zh: 厥咎狂，厥罰恒雨，厥極惡。

translations.literal: Its fault is madness, its punishment constant rain, its extreme wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Its fault is madness, its punishment constant rain, its extreme wickedness.

sentences.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，時則有雞禍，時則有下體生上之痾，時則有青眚、青祥。

translations.literal: At times there are costume prodigies; at times turtle calamities; at times chicken disasters; at times ailments of the lower body growing on the upper; at times green internal misfortune and green auguries.
translations.idiomatic: At times there are costume prodigies; at times turtle calamities; at times chicken disasters; at times ailments of the lower body growing on the upper; at times green internal misfortune and green auguries.

sentences.zh: 惟金沴木。

translations.literal: Only metal encroaches upon wood.
translations.idiomatic: Only metal encroaches upon wood.

sentences.zh: 」班固曰：「蓋工匠為輪矢者多傷敗，及木為變怪。

translations.literal: " Ban Gu said: "Generally when craftsmen make wheels and arrows many are damaged and ruined, and when wood becomes strange anomalies —
translations.idiomatic: " Ban Gu said: "Generally when craftsmen make wheels and arrows many are damaged and ruined, and when wood becomes strange anomalies —

sentences.zh: 」皆為不曲直也。

translations.literal: " all of these are wood losing its bending and straightening."
translations.idiomatic: " all of these are wood losing its bending and straightening."

sentences.zh: 木不曲直

translations.literal: Wood Loses Its Bending and Straightening
translations.idiomatic: Wood Loses Its Straightness and Suppleness

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初六年正月，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, there was rain and trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, rain fell and encased the trees in ice.

sentences.zh: 接劉歆說，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: Following Liu Xin's explanation, this was wood losing its bending and straightening.
translations.idiomatic: Following Liu Xin's explanation, this was wood losing its straightness and suppleness.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「冰者陰之盛，木者少陽，貴臣象也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: "Ice is the flourishing of Yin; wood is lesser Yang; it is the image of honored ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said: "Ice is the flourishing of Yin; wood is lesser Yang; it is the image of honored ministers.

sentences.zh: 此人將有害，則陰氣脅木，木先寒，故得雨而冰也。

translations.literal: When this person is about to suffer harm, then Yin qi coerces wood; wood first becomes cold; therefore it obtains rain and ice."
translations.idiomatic: When such an official faces mortal peril, Yin first presses upon wood's Yang; the timber turns chill before the freezing rain seals it."

sentences.zh: 」是年六月，利成郡兵蔡方等殺太守徐質，據郡反，多所脅略，并聚亡命。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, soldiers of Licheng commandery, Cai Fang and others, killed Administrator Xu Zhi, held the commandery in rebellion, coerced and plundered widely, and gathered together fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month the Licheng garrison under Cai Fang murdered Prefect Xu Zhi and seized the commandery in revolt, coercing and plundering widely and gathering fugitives.

sentences.zh: 遣二校尉與青州刺史共討平之。

translations.literal: Two commandants were dispatched together with the Inspector of Qing Province to campaign against them and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Two commandants were dispatched together with the Inspector of Qing Province to campaign against them and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 太守，古之諸侯，貴臣有害之應也。

translations.literal: The administrator is the feudal lord of antiquity — the response of honored ministers suffering harm.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery governor ranked as a feudal lord of old — precisely the ministerial token Liu Xiang had named.

sentences.zh: 一說以木冰為甲兵之象。

translations.literal: One explanation takes icing on trees as the image of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Another explanation takes glazed branches as the image of armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 是歲，既討蔡方，又八月，天子自將以舟師征吳，戎卒十餘萬，連旍數百里，臨江觀兵。

translations.literal: That year, having already campaigned against Cai Fang, again in the eighth month the Son of Heaven personally led a naval force to campaign against Wu; garrison troops were over a hundred thousand; connected banners stretched several hundred li; viewing troops along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The same year saw Cai Fang crushed; then in the eighth month the emperor personally led a river fleet against Wu — more than a hundred thousand men and banners unbroken for hundreds of li massed along the bank.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興三年二月辛未，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, on the day xinwei of the second month, there was rain and trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the second month in the third year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin came freezing rain and ice-rimed trees.

sentences.zh: 後二年，周顗、戴淵、刁協、劉隗皆遇害，與春秋同事，是其應也。

translations.literal: Two years later, Zhou Yi, Dai Yuan, Diao Xie, and Liu Kui all met harm — the same sort of affair as in the Spring and Autumn Annals; this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Zhou Yi, Dai Yuan, Diao Xie, and Liu Kui were all killed — the same sort of affair as in the Spring and Autumn Annals; this was its response.

sentences.zh: 一曰，是後王敦攻京師，又其象也。

translations.literal: One account says: afterward Wang Dun attacked the capital — this too was its portent.
translations.idiomatic: One account says: afterward Wang Dun attacked the capital — this too was its portent.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和八年正月乙巳，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, on the day yisi of the first month, there was rain and trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the first month in the eighth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, rain fell and trees froze over.

sentences.zh: 是年，殷浩北伐，明年，軍敗，十年，廢黜。

translations.literal: That year Yin Hao campaigned north; the next year the army was defeated; in the tenth year he was dismissed and degraded.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao marched north that year; his army collapsed the next, and within ten years he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 又曰，荀羨、殷浩北伐，桓溫入關之象也。

translations.literal: It is also said: Xun Xian and Yin Hao campaigned north — this was the portent of Huan Wen entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators also tie the sign to Xun Xian's and Yin Hao's northern expeditions — the prelude to Huan Wen's thrust into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十四年十二月乙巳，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, on the day yisi of the twelfth month, there was rain and trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the twelfth month in the fourteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, freezing rain glazed the trees.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，王恭為北蕃；

translations.literal: The next year in the second month Wang Gong became northern bulwark;
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Wang Gong took charge of the northern marches;

sentences.zh: 八月，庾楷為西蕃；

translations.literal: in the eighth month Yu Kai became western bulwark;
translations.idiomatic: by the eighth month Yu Kai held the western frontier;

sentences.zh: 九月，王國寶為中書令，尋加領軍將軍；

translations.literal: in the ninth month Wang Guobao became Palace Writer and soon added command of the guards;
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month Wang Guobao entered the Palace Secretariat, soon adding command of the capital guards;

sentences.zh: 十七年殷仲堪為荊州。

translations.literal: in the seventeenth year Yin Zhongkan became Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: within seventeen years Yin Zhongkan gained Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 雖邪正異規，而終同摧滅，是其應也。

translations.literal: Although wicked and upright followed different plans, in the end alike they were exterminated together — this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Rival camps clashed in principle yet every faction was annihilated alike — this was its response.

sentences.zh: 一曰，苻堅雖敗，關、河未一，丁零鮮卑，侵略司、兗，竇揚勝扇逼梁、雍，兵役不已，又其象也。

translations.literal: One account says: although Fu Jian was defeated, the passes and rivers were not yet unified; the Dingling and Xianbei invaded Si and Yan; Dou Yangsheng fanned rebellion and pressed Liang and Yong; military corvées did not cease — this too was its portent.
translations.idiomatic: One account says: although Fu Jian was defeated, the passes and rivers were not yet unified; the Dingling and Xianbei invaded Si and Yan; Dou Yangsheng fanned rebellion and pressed Liang and Yong; military corvées did not cease — this too was its portent.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮建興二年，諸葛恪征淮南，行後，所坐聽事棟中折。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianxing under Sun Liang of Wu, when Zhuge Ke campaigned against Huainan, after he set out the ridgepole of the hall where he sat broke in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianxing under Sun Liang of Wu, after Zhuge Ke marched against Huainan the central beam of his audience hall snapped.

sentences.zh: 恪妄興徵役，奪民農時，作為邪謀，傷國財力，故木失其性，致毀折也。

translations.literal: Ke rashly raised campaigns and corvées, seized the people's farming seasons, enacted evil plots, and harmed the state's wealth and strength — therefore wood lost its nature and reached destruction and breakage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke had stirred needless wars, seized the farming calendar, and spun treasonous schemes that drained the realm — wood therefore abandoned its nature and shattered his hall.

sentences.zh: 及旋師而誅滅，於周易又為棟橈之凶也。

translations.literal: When he turned the army and was executed and extinguished, in the Zhou Changes it was again "the misfortune of a ridgepole bent."
translations.idiomatic: His retreat ended in execution and clan extinction — the Zhou yi calls such collapse the ill omen of the sagging ridgepole.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康五年五月，宣帝廟地陷梁折。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, the earth of Emperor Xuan's temple sank and beams broke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, the floor of Emperor Xuan's temple subsided and its beams gave way.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，太廟殿又陷，改作廟，築基及泉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the Grand Temple hall again sank; they rebuilt the temple, digging the foundation down to the springs.
translations.idiomatic: The first month of the eighth year brought another collapse of the imperial ancestral hall; builders dug a new foundation to the water table.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，遂更營新廟，遠致名材，雜以銅柱。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month they then built anew a temple at distance, bringing celebrated timbers and mixing in bronze pillars.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they raised a new shrine elsewhere, importing prized lumber and bronze columns.

sentences.zh: 陳勰為匠，作者六萬人。

translations.literal: Chen Xie was master craftsman; those who worked were sixty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xie directed sixty thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，乃成。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The structure stood finished in the tenth year's fourth month.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚寅，梁又折。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on the day gengyin the beams again broke.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on gengyin in the eleventh month the beams snapped again.

sentences.zh: 按地陷者，分離之象，梁折者，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: According to this, sinking earth is the image of division and separation; breaking beams is wood losing its bending and straightening.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's lesson read partition into the sinking soil and wood's failed office into the splintered beams.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：于時後宮殿有孽火，又廟梁無故自折。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: At that time there was calamitous fire in the rear palace halls, and the temple beams again broke without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng said: At that time there was calamitous fire in the rear palace halls, and the temple beams again broke without cause.

sentences.zh: 先是帝多不豫，益惡之。

translations.literal: Before this the emperor had often been unwell and grew all the more troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the emperor had often been unwell and grew all the more troubled by it.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝崩，而王室頻亂，遂亡天下。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died, and the royal house repeatedly fell into chaos and in the end lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died the next year, and the royal house repeatedly fell into chaos and in the end lost the realm.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，成都王穎使陸機率眾向京師，擊長沙王乂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an under Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying had Lu Ji lead forces toward the capital to strike the Prince of Changsha Sima Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tai'an under Emperor Hui of Jin, Prince Chengdu Sima Ying sent Lu Ji against Prince Changsha Sima Yi at the capital.

sentences.zh: 軍始引而牙竿折，俄而戰敗，機被誅。

translations.literal: When the army had just set out the banner pole snapped; shortly they were defeated in battle; Lu Ji was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The host had barely marched when the standard mast splintered — soon Lu Ji fell defeated and was executed.

sentences.zh: 穎尋奔潰，卒賜死。

translations.literal: Ying then fled in collapse and in the end was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's army melted away, and he himself was ultimately compelled to suicide.

sentences.zh: 初，河間王顒謀先誅長沙，廢太子，立穎。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Hejian Sima Yong had plotted first to execute the Prince of Changsha, depose the crown prince, and install Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Hejian Sima Yong had plotted first to execute Prince Changsha, depose the crown prince, and install Ying.

sentences.zh: 長沙知之，誅其黨卞粹等，故穎來伐。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha learned of it and executed his faction, Bian Cui and others — therefore Ying came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changsha learned of it and executed his faction, Bian Cui and others — therefore Ying came to attack.

sentences.zh: 機又以穎得遐邇心，將為漢之代王，遂委質於穎，為犯從之將。

translations.literal: Lu Ji also, because Ying had won the hearts of near and far and would become a replacement king for Han, then submitted to Ying and became a general in the ranks of the accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji also, because Ying had won the hearts of near and far and would become a replacement king for Han, then submitted to Ying and became a general in the ranks of the accomplice.

sentences.zh: 此皆姦謀之罰，木不曲直也。

translations.literal: All of these were punishments for treacherous plotting — wood losing its bending and straightening.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punished the conspiracy by stripping wood of its bend-and-straight virtue.

sentences.zh: 王敦在武昌，鈴下儀仗生華如蓮花狀，五六日而萎落。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun was at Wuchang, halberds and paraphernalia under the guard sprouted blossoms like lotus flowers; after five or six days they withered and fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun was at Wuchang, halberds and paraphernalia under the guard sprouted blossoms like lotus flowers; after five or six days they withered and fell.

sentences.zh: 此木失其性而為變也。

translations.literal: This was wood losing its nature and becoming a transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Wood had plainly forfeited its proper nature and become a transformation.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「鈴閤，尊貴者之儀；

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "The bell pavilion is the ritual of the honored;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao said: "The bell pavilion is the ritual of the honored;

sentences.zh: 鈴下，主威儀之官。

translations.literal: those under the bell are officials who maintain awe-inspiring bearing.
translations.idiomatic: those under the bell are officials who maintain awe-inspiring bearing.

sentences.zh: 今狂花生於枯木，又在鈴閤之間，言威儀之富，榮華之盛，皆如狂花之發，不可久也。

translations.literal: Now mad blossoms grow on dead wood, moreover within the bell pavilion — this speaks of the fullness of awe-inspiring ritual and the flourishing of glory and splendor, all like the blooming of mad blossoms, unable to endure long."
translations.idiomatic: Now freak blossoms grow on dead timber beside the headquarters bell — this speaks of the fullness of awe-inspiring ritual and the flourishing of glory and splendor, all flashing as briefly as those unnatural flowers."

sentences.zh: 」其後終以逆命，沒又加戮，是其應也。

translations.literal: Afterward he in the end by disobedient mandate met ruin, and after death corporal punishment was added — this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun later died in rebellion and suffered posthumous mutilation for defying the throne — this was its response.

sentences.zh: 一說此花孽也，於周易為「枯楊生華」。

translations.literal: One explanation takes this as the calamity of blossoms; in the Zhou Changes it is "withered poplar sprouts blossoms."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading classes it among floral prodigies — the Zhou yi image of fresh blossoms on a withered poplar.

sentences.zh: 桓玄始篡，龍旂竿折。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan first usurped, the dragon-banner pole snapped.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan Xuan seized the throne, the great dragon standard broke.

sentences.zh: 玄田獵出入，不絕昏夜，飲食恣奢，土水妨農，又多姦謀，故木失其性也。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan hunted in coming and going without cease day and night, ate and drank extravagantly, earth and water works harmed farming, and there were many treacherous plots — therefore wood lost its nature.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted without restraint day and night, feasted extravagantly, and pressed construction works that tore peasants from their fields while intrigue multiplied — wood therefore lost its nature.

sentences.zh: 夫旂所以擬三辰，章著明也。

translations.literal: The banner is what displays the three luminaries and manifests brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The banner displays the Three Lights of sovereignty and manifests brightness.

sentences.zh: 旂竿之折，高明去矣。

translations.literal: Breaking the banner pole means the lofty brightness departs.
translations.idiomatic: A shattered mast meant manifest legitimacy had departed.

sentences.zh: 在位八十日而敗。

translations.literal: He held office eighty days and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He held office eighty days and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始二年五月丙午，南琅邪臨沂黃城山道士盛道度堂屋一柱自然，夜光照室內。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, on the day bingwu of the fifth month, at Huangcheng Mountain in Linyi, Nanlangya, the Daoist Sheng Daodu's hall had one pillar spontaneously glow, its light illuminating the chamber at night.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day in the fifth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, at Huangcheng Mountain in Linyi, Nanlangya, one pillar of the Daoist Sheng Daodu's hall spontaneously glowed, its light illuminating the chamber at night.

sentences.zh: 此木失其性也。

translations.literal: This was wood losing its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Wood had plainly lost its nature.

sentences.zh: 或云木腐自光。

translations.literal: Some say rotted wood naturally glows.
translations.idiomatic: Some say rotted wood naturally glows.

sentences.zh: 廢帝昇明元年，吳興餘杭舍亭禾蕈樹生李實。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming under the Deposed Emperor, at Sheting in Yuhang, Wuxing, a hetong tree bore plum fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming under the Deposed Emperor, at Sheting in Yuhang, Wuxing, a hetong tree bore plum fruit.

sentences.zh: 禾蕈樹，民間所謂胡頹樹。

translations.literal: The hetong tree is what the common people call the hutui tree.
translations.idiomatic: The hetong tree is what the common people call the hutui tree.

sentences.zh: 貌不恭

translations.literal: Improper Bearing
translations.idiomatic: Bearing Lacks Respect

sentences.zh: 魏文帝居諒闇之始，便數出遊獵體，貌不重，風尚通脫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's period of mourning for his father, he repeatedly went out hunting and sporting; his bearing lacked weight; the prevailing fashion favored easy unconventionality.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Wei's period of mourning for his father, he repeatedly went out hunting and sporting; his bearing lacked weight; the prevailing fashion favored easy unconventionality.

sentences.zh: 故戴凌以直諫抵罪，鮑勛以迕旨極刑。

translations.literal: Therefore Dai Ling suffered punishment for direct remonstrance, and Bao Xun received the extreme penalty for opposing the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Dai Ling suffered punishment for direct remonstrance, and Bao Xun received the extreme penalty for opposing the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 天下化之，咸賤守節，此貌之不恭也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven were transformed by it and alike despised maintaining propriety — this was bearing lacking respect.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven were transformed by it and alike despised maintaining propriety — this was bearing lacking respect.

sentences.zh: 是以享國不永，後祚短促。

translations.literal: Therefore his enjoyment of the realm was not long-lasting and the later fortune was brief.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore his enjoyment of the realm was not long-lasting and the later fortune was brief.

sentences.zh: 春秋魯君居喪不哀，在慼而有嘉容，穆叔謂之不度，後終出奔。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, the lord of Lu during mourning was not mournful; while in grief he yet had a pleasing countenance; Mu Shu called this lacking measure, and afterward he finally fled into exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, the lord of Lu during mourning was not mournful; while in grief he yet had a pleasing countenance; Mu Shu called this lacking measure, and afterward he finally fled into exile.

sentences.zh: 蓋同事也。

translations.literal: Generally it was the same sort of affair.
translations.idiomatic: Generally it was the same sort of affair.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書鄧颺，行步弛縱，筋不束體，坐起傾倚，若無手足。

translations.literal: Deng Yang of Wei, Master of Writing, walked loose-limbed and reckless — sinews not binding the body; sitting and rising he leaned and slouched as if without hands or feet.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang of Wei, Master of Writing, walked loose-limbed and reckless — sinews not binding the body; sitting and rising he leaned and slouched as if without hands or feet.

sentences.zh: 此貌之不恭也。

translations.literal: This was bearing lacking respect.
translations.idiomatic: This was bearing lacking respect.

sentences.zh: 管輅謂之鬼躁。

translations.literal: Guan Lu called it ghost restlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu called it ghost restlessness.

sentences.zh: 鬼躁者，凶終之徵。

translations.literal: Ghost restlessness is a sign of a violent end.
translations.idiomatic: Ghost restlessness is a sign of a violent end.

sentences.zh: 後卒誅死。

translations.literal: Later he was executed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed and died.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，貴遊子弟相與為散髮倮身之飲，對弄婢妾。

translations.literal: During the Yuankang era under Emperor Hui of Jin, sons of noble families together held drinking parties with disheveled hair and naked bodies, sporting with servant girls and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuankang era under Emperor Hui of Jin, sons of noble families held drinking parties with hair loose and bodies bare, sporting with servant girls and concubines.

sentences.zh: 逆之者傷好，非之者負譏。

translations.literal: Those who resisted were wounded in friendship; those who disapproved bore ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Those who resisted lost friends; those who disapproved bore ridicule.

sentences.zh: 希世之士，恥不與焉。

translations.literal: Men aspiring to worldly fame were ashamed not to join in.
translations.idiomatic: Men who craved renown were ashamed not to join in.

sentences.zh: 蓋胡、翟侵中國之萌也。

translations.literal: This was surely the sprouting of the Hu and Di encroaching upon Central China.
translations.idiomatic: This was surely the first sprouting of Hu and Di encroachment upon the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 豈徒伊川之民，一被髮而祭者乎。

translations.literal: Was it not merely like the people of the Yi River, who once let down their hair and offered sacrifices?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not merely like the people of the Yi River, who once let down their hair and offered sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，賈謐親貴，數入二宮，與儲君遊戲，无降下心。

translations.literal: During Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, Jia Mi was close and honored; he repeatedly entered the two palaces and played with the crown prince, without a subordinate's demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, Jia Mi stood close to power; he repeatedly entered the two palaces to play with the crown prince, showing none of a subject's deference.

sentences.zh: 又嘗同弈棊爭道，成都王穎厲色曰：「皇太子，國之儲貳。

translations.literal: Once when they played go together and disputed the board, Prince Chengdu Sima Ying said sternly: "The crown prince is the state's heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Once when they played go together and disputed the board, Prince Chengdu Sima Ying said sternly: "The crown prince is the heir to the realm.

sentences.zh: 賈謐何敢無禮！

translations.literal: How dare Jia Mi act without propriety!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare Jia Mi act without propriety!"

sentences.zh: 」謐猶不悛，故及於禍。

translations.literal: Yet Mi still did not repent, and therefore met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Mi still would not repent, and therefore met disaster.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏既誅趙倫，因留輔政，坐拜百官，符敕臺府，淫醟專驕，不一朝覲。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Sima Jiong, having executed Zhao Lun, remained to assist in government; he received bows while seated, issued orders to the central offices, indulged in wine and pride, and did not once attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Sima Jiong, having executed Zhao Lun, stayed on to govern; he accepted bows while seated, issued orders to the central offices, drowned himself in wine and pride, and never once attended court.

sentences.zh: 此狂恣不肅之容也。

translations.literal: This was the bearing of reckless insolence without solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: This was the bearing of reckless insolence without solemnity.

sentences.zh: 天下莫不高其功，而慮其亡也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven praised his achievement yet feared his destruction.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven praised his achievement yet feared his downfall.

sentences.zh: 冏終弗改，遂至夷滅。

translations.literal: Jiong in the end did not reform, and was utterly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong never reformed, and was utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 太元中，人不復著帩頭。

translations.literal: During the Taiyuan era, people no longer wore the zhatou headwrap.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan era, people ceased wearing the zhatou headwrap.

sentences.zh: 頭者，元首，帩者，令髮不垂，助元首為儀飾者也。

translations.literal: The head is the chief; the zhatou keeps the hair from hanging loose and assists the chief as ritual adornment.
translations.idiomatic: The head is the sovereign part; the zhatou keeps the hair from falling loose and assists the head as ritual adornment.

sentences.zh: 今忽廢之，若人君獨立無輔，以至危亡也。

translations.literal: Now it was suddenly abandoned — as if the sovereign stood alone without ministers, leading to peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Now it was suddenly cast aside — as if the ruler stood alone without ministers, leading to peril and ruin.

sentences.zh: 其後桓玄篡位。

translations.literal: Afterward Huan Xuan usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Huan Xuan usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 舊為屐者，齒皆達楄上，名曰「露卯」。

translations.literal: Formerly when making wooden clogs, the teeth reached the upper frame, called "exposed mortise."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when making wooden clogs, the pegs reached the upper frame — they were called "exposed mortise."

sentences.zh: 太元中，忽不徹，名曰「陰卯」。

translations.literal: During Taiyuan they suddenly stopped finishing them through, calling them "hidden mortise."
translations.idiomatic: During Taiyuan they suddenly stopped driving the pegs through, calling them "hidden mortise."

sentences.zh: 其後多陰謀，遂致大亂。

translations.literal: Afterward conspiracies multiplied and great chaos ensued.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward conspiracies multiplied and the realm fell into great chaos.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙七年，晉朝拜授劉毅世子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, the Jin court invested Liu Yi's heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, the Jin court invested Liu Yi's heir.

sentences.zh: 毅以王命之重，當設饗宴親，請吏佐臨視。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, considering the weight of the royal mandate, should have held a feast for kinsmen and invited officials to witness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, considering the weight of the royal mandate, ought to have held a feast for his kinsmen and invited his officers to witness.

sentences.zh: 至日，國僚不重白，默拜於廄中。

translations.literal: On the day, his state retainers did not report properly and performed the obeisance in silence in the stable.
translations.idiomatic: On the day, his state retainers failed to announce the rite properly and performed the obeisance in silence in the stable.

sentences.zh: 王人將反命，毅方知，大以為恨，免郎中令劉敬叔官。

translations.literal: When the court envoy was about to report back, Yi only then learned of it; he resented this deeply and dismissed Gentleman of the Palace Liu Jingshu from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the court envoy was about to report back, Yi only then learned of it; he resented this deeply and stripped Gentleman of the Palace Liu Jingshu of his post.

sentences.zh: 識者怪焉。

translations.literal: Those who understood were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood were astonished.

sentences.zh: 此墮略嘉禮，不肅之妖也。

translations.literal: This was a prodigy of neglecting excellent ritual and lacking solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: This was a prodigy of neglecting excellent ritual and lacking solemnity.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝靈運有逸才，每出入，自扶接者常數人。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun of Chen Commandery had exceptional talent; whenever he went out or in, several men supported him by the arms.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun of Chen Commandery had exceptional talent; whenever he went out or in, several men supported him by the arms.

sentences.zh: 民間謠曰「四人挈衣裙，三人捉坐席」是也。

translations.literal: A folk song said, "Four men carry gown and skirt, three men hold the seat" — this was it.
translations.idiomatic: A folk song ran, "Four men carry gown and skirt, three men hold the seat" — this was it.

sentences.zh: 此蓋不肅之咎，後坐誅。

translations.literal: This was surely the fault of lacking solemnity; afterward he was executed for it.
translations.idiomatic: This was surely the fault of lacking solemnity; afterward he was executed for it.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始中，幸臣阮佃夫勢傾朝廷，室宇豪麗，車服鮮明，乘車常偏向一邊，違正立執綏之體。

translations.literal: During the Taishi era under Emperor Ming of Song, the favorite minister Ruan Tianfu's power tilted the court; his halls were sumptuous, his carriages and vestments brilliant; riding he constantly leaned to one side, violating the proper posture of standing erect and holding the reins.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era under Emperor Ming of Song, the favorite Ruan Tianfu's power tilted the court; his halls were sumptuous, his carriages and vestments brilliant; when he rode he constantly leaned to one side, violating the upright posture of standing square and holding the reins.

sentences.zh: 時人多慕效。

translations.literal: Many people at the time admired and imitated this.
translations.idiomatic: Many at the time admired and copied him.

sentences.zh: 此亦貌不恭之失也。

translations.literal: This too was the fault of unseemly bearing.
translations.idiomatic: This too was bearing lacking respect.

sentences.zh: 時偏左之化行，方正之道廢矣。

translations.literal: The fashion of leaning left spread; the way of uprightness and squareness was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The fashion of leaning left spread; the way of uprightness and squareness was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝常單騎遊遨，出入市里營寺，未嘗御輦。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor often rode alone on excursions, entering and leaving markets, wards, and monasteries, never using the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor often rode alone on excursions, passing through markets, wards, and monasteries, never using the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 終以殞滅。

translations.literal: In the end he met destruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he met destruction.

sentences.zh: 恒雨

translations.literal: Constant Rain
translations.idiomatic: Constant Rain

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和元年秋，數大雨，多暴雷電，非常，至殺鳥雀。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei, heavy rains fell repeatedly with violent thunder and lightning — something extraordinary, even killing birds.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the first year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei, heavy rains fell again and again with violent thunder and lightning — something extraordinary, even killing birds.

sentences.zh: 案楊阜上蔬，此桓雨之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Yang Fu's memorial, this was the punishment of constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: According to Yang Fu's memorial, this was the punishment of constant rain.

sentences.zh: 時帝居喪不哀，出入弋獵無度，奢侈繁興，奪民農時，故木失其性而恒雨為災也。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was not mournful during mourning; he went out hunting without limit; extravagance flourished; he seized the people's farming seasons — therefore wood lost its nature and constant rain became disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was not mournful during mourning; he hunted without restraint; extravagance flourished; he seized the people's farming seasons — therefore wood lost its nature and constant rain became disaster.

sentences.zh: 太和四年八月，大雨霖三十餘日，伊、洛、河、漢皆溢，歲以凶饑。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe came incessant rain for more than thirty days; the Yi, Luo, Yellow, and Han rivers all overflowed, and the year brought famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe came incessant rain for more than thirty days; the Yi, Luo, Yellow, and Han rivers all overflowed, and the year brought famine.

sentences.zh: 孫亮太平二年二月甲寅，大雨震電；

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping under Sun Liang of Wu, on jiayin of the second month, heavy rain and thunder;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping under Sun Liang of Wu, on jiayin of the second month, heavy rain and thunder;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，雪，大寒。

translations.literal: on yimao, snow and severe cold.
translations.idiomatic: on yimao, snow and severe cold.

sentences.zh: 案劉歆說，此時當雨而不當大，大雨，恒雨之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xin's explanation, at this time there should have been rain but not so much — heavy rain is the punishment of constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: According to Liu Xin's explanation, at this season there should have been rain but not so much — heavy rain is the punishment of constant rain.

sentences.zh: 於始震電之明日而雪大寒，又恒寒之罰也。

translations.literal: That snow and severe cold came the day after the first thunder was also the punishment of constant cold.
translations.idiomatic: That snow and severe cold came the day after the first thunder was also the punishment of constant cold.

sentences.zh: 劉向以為既已震電，則雪不當復降，皆失時之異也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang held that once thunder had occurred, snow ought not to fall again — all were anomalies out of season.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang held that once thunder had sounded, snow ought not to fall again — all were anomalies out of season.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，為君失時，賊臣將起。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the ruler has lost the season; a rebel minister will rise.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the ruler has lost the season; a rebel minister will rise.

sentences.zh: 先震電而後雪者，陰見間隙，起而勝陽。

translations.literal: Thunder first and snow afterward means Yin saw an opening and rose to overcome Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder first and snow afterward means Yin saw an opening and rose to overcome Yang.

sentences.zh: 逆殺之禍將及也。

translations.literal: The calamity of treacherous killing was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity of treacherous killing was about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 亮不悟，尋見廢。

translations.literal: Liang did not understand; soon he was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang did not understand; soon he was deposed.

sentences.zh: 此與春秋魯隱同也。

translations.literal: This was the same as Duke Yin of Lu in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: This was the same as Duke Yin of Lu in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始六年六月，大雨霖，甲辰，河、洛、沁水同時並溢，流四千九百餘家，殺二百餘人，沒秋稼千三百六十餘頃。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin came incessant rain; on jiachen the Yellow, Luo, and Qin rivers overflowed together, sweeping away more than four thousand nine hundred households, killing more than two hundred people, and drowning more than thirteen hundred sixty qing of autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin came incessant rain; on jiachen the Yellow, Luo, and Qin rivers overflowed together, sweeping away more than four thousand nine hundred households, killing more than two hundred people, and drowning more than thirteen hundred sixty qing of autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 晉武太康五年七月，任城、梁國暴雨，害豆麥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, torrential rain in Rencheng and Liang struck beans and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, torrential rain in Rencheng and Liang struck beans and wheat.

sentences.zh: 太康五年九月，南安霖雨暴雪，折樹木，害秋稼；

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Taikang, incessant rain and sudden snow in Nan'an broke trees and harmed autumn grain;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Taikang, incessant rain and sudden snow in Nan'an broke trees and harmed autumn grain;

sentences.zh: 魏郡、淮南、平原雨水，傷秋稼。

translations.literal: in Wei, Huainan, and Pingyuan, rain and flood harmed autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: in Wei, Huainan, and Pingyuan, rain and flood harmed autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 是秋，魏郡、西平郡九縣霖雨暴水，霜傷秋稼。

translations.literal: That autumn, incessant rain and sudden flood in nine counties of Wei and Xiping, with frost, harmed autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, incessant rain and sudden flood in nine counties of Wei and Xiping, with frost, harmed autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永寧元年十月，義陽、南陽、東海霖雨，淹害秋麥。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning under Emperor Hui of Jin, incessant rain in Yiyang, Nanyang, and Donghai flooded and harmed autumn wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning under Emperor Hui of Jin, incessant rain in Yiyang, Nanyang, and Donghai flooded and harmed autumn wheat.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康元年八月乙丑，荊州之長沙攸、醴陵、武陵之龍陽三縣，雨水浮漂屋室，殺人，傷損秋稼。

translations.literal: On yichou of the eighth month in the first year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, in the three counties of Changsha, You, and Longyang in Wuling of Jing Province, floodwaters floated houses, killed people, and harmed autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou of the eighth month in the first year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, in the three counties of Changsha, You, and Longyang in Wuling of Jing Province, floodwaters floated houses, killed people, and harmed autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十一年六月，京邑連雨百餘日，大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the capital saw rain for more than a hundred consecutive days and great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the capital saw rain for more than a hundred consecutive days and great flood.

sentences.zh: 何晏服婦人之服，亦亡其家。
其咎均也。
吳婦人之修容者，急束其髮，而劘角過于耳。
蓋其俗自操束大急，而廉隅失中之謂也。
故吳之風俗，相驅以急，言論彈射，以刻薄相尚。
居三年之喪者，往往有致毀以死。
諸葛患之，著正交論，雖不可以經訓整亂，蓋亦救時之作也。
孫休後，衣服之制，上長下短，又積領五六而裳居一二。
干寶曰：「上饒奢，下儉逼，上有餘下不足之妖也。
」至孫晧，果奢暴恣情於上，而百姓彫困於下，卒以亡國。
是其應也。
晉興後，衣服上儉下豐，著衣者皆厭䙅蓋裙。
君衰弱，臣放縱，下掩上之象也。
陵遲至元康末，婦人出兩襠，加乎脛之上，此內出外也。
為車乘者，苟貴輕細，又數變易其形，皆以白篾為純，古喪車之遺象。
乘者，君子之器，蓋君子立心無恒，事不崇實也。
干寶曰：「及晉之禍，天子失柄，權制寵臣，下掩上之應也。
永嘉末，六宮才人，流徙戎、翟，內出外之應也。
及天下亂擾，宰輔方伯，多負其任，又數改易，不崇實之應也。」
晉武帝泰始後，中國相尚用胡牀、貊盤，及為羌煑、貊炙。
貴人富室，必置其器，吉享嘉會，皆此為先。
太康中，天下又以氈為絈頭及絡帶、衿口。
百姓相戲曰，中國必為胡所破也。
氈產於胡，而天下以為絈頭、帶身、衿口，胡既三制之矣，能无敗乎。
干寶曰：「元康中，氐、羌反，至于永嘉，劉淵、石勒遂有中都。
自後四夷迭據華土，是其應也。」
晉武帝太康後，天下為家者，移婦人於東方，空萊北庭，以為園囿。
干寶曰：「夫王朝南向，正陽也；
后北宮，位太陰也；
世子居東宮，位少陽也。
今居內於東，是與外俱南面也。
亢陽无陰，婦人失位而干少陽之象也。
賈后讒戮愍懷，俄而禍敗亦及。」
昔初作履者，婦人圓頭，男子方頭。
圓者，順從之義，所以別男女也。
晉太康初，婦人皆履方頭，此去其圓從，與男無別也。
太康之中，天下為晉世寧之舞，手接杯槃反覆之，歌曰：「晉世寧，舞杯槃。
」夫樂生人心，所以觀事。
故記曰：「總干山立，武王之事也；
發揚蹈厲，太公之志也；
武亂皆坐，周、召之治也。
」又曰：「其治民勞者，舞行綴遠；
其治民逸者，舞行綴近。
今接杯槃於手上而反覆之，至危也。
杯槃者，酒食之器也，而名曰晉世寧者，言晉世之士，偷苟於酒食之間，而其知不及遠，晉世之寧，猶杯槃之在手也。」
晉惠帝元康中，婦人之飾有五兵佩，又以金、銀、瑇瑁之屬為斧、鉞、戈、戟，以當笄□。
干寶曰：「男女之別，國之大節，故服物異等，贄幣不同。
今婦人而以兵器為飾，又妖之大也。
遂有賈后之事，終以兵亡天下。」
元康中，婦人結髮者，既成，以繒急束其環，名曰擷子紒。
始自中宮，天下化之。
其後賈后果害太子。
元康中，天下始相倣為㮧杖，以柱掖其後，稍施其錞，住則植之。
夫木，東方之行，金之臣也。
扶者，杖體之器，㮧其頭者，尤便用也。
必傍柱掖者，傍救之象也。
王室多故，而元帝以蕃臣樹德東方，維持天下，柱掖之應也。
至社稷無主，海內歸之，遂承天命，建都江外，獨立之應也。
元康末至太安間，江、淮之域，有敗編自聚于道，多者或至四五十量。
干寶嘗使人散而去之，或投林草，或投坑谷。
明日視之，悉復如故。
民或云見狸銜而聚之，亦未察也。
寶說曰：「夫編者，人之賤服，最處于下，而當勞辱，下民之象也。
敗者，疲斃之象也。
道者，地理四方，所以交通王命所由往來也。
故今敗編聚於道者，象下民罷病，將相聚為亂，絕四方而壅王命之象也。
在位者莫察。
太安中，發壬午兵，百姓嗟怨。
江夏男子張昌遂首亂荊楚，從之者如流。
於是兵革歲起，天下因之，遂大破壞。
此近服妖也。」
晉孝懷永嘉以來，士大夫竟服生箋單衣。
遠識者怪之，竊指擿曰：「此則古者繐衰之布，諸侯大夫所以服天子也。
今無故畢服之，殆有應乎？
」其後愍、懷晏駕，不獲厥所。
晉元帝太興以來，兵士以絳囊縛紒。
紒在首，莫上焉。
周易乾為首，坤為囊。
坤，臣道也。
晉金行，赤火色，金之賊也。
以朱囊縛紒，臣道上侵之象也。
到永昌元年，大將軍王敦舉兵內攻，六軍散潰。
舊為羽扇，柄刻木，象其骨形，羽用十，取全數也。
晉中興初，王敦南征，始改為長柄下出，可捉，而減其羽用八。
識者尤之曰：「夫羽扇，翼之名也。
創為長柄者，執其柄制羽翼也。
以十改八者，將以未備奪已備也。
」是時為衣者，又上短，帶至于掖；
著帽者，以帶縛項。
下逼上，上無地也。
下袴者，直幅為口無殺，下大失裁也。
尋有兵亂，三年而再攻京師。
晉海西初嗣位，迎官忘設豹尾。
識者以為不終之象，近服妖也。
晉司馬道子於府北園內為酒鑪列肆，使姬人酤鬻酒肴，如裨販者，數遊其中，身自買易，因醉寓寢，動連日夜。
漢靈帝嘗若此。
干寶以為：「君將失位，降在皁隸之象也。
」道子卒見廢徙，以庶人終。
桓玄篡立，殿上施絳綾帳，鏤黃金為顏，四角金龍，銜五色羽葆流蘇。
羣下竊相謂曰：「頗類輀車。
」此服妖也。
晉末皆冠小冠，而衣裳博大，風流相倣，輿臺成俗。
識者曰：「此禪代之象也。
」永初以後，冠還大云。
宋文帝元嘉六年，民間婦人結髮者，三分髮，抽其鬟直向上，謂之「飛天紒」。
始自東府，流被民庶。
時司徒彭城王義康居東府，其後卒以陵上徙廢。
孝武帝世，豫州刺史劉德願善御車，世祖嘗使之御畫輪，幸太宰江夏王義恭第。
德願挾牛杖催世祖云：「日暮宜歸！
」又求益僦車。
世祖甚歡。
此事與漢靈帝西園蓄私錢同也。
孝武世，幸臣戴法興權亞人主，造圓頭履，世人莫不效之。
其時圓進之俗大行，方格之風盡矣。
明帝初，司徒建安王休仁統軍赭圻，制烏紗帽，反抽帽裙，民間謂之「司徒狀」，京邑翕然相尚。
休仁後果以疑逼致禍。
龜孽
晉惠帝永熙初，衛瓘家人炊飯，墮地，盡化為螺，出足起行。
螺，龜類，近龜孽也。
干寶曰：「螺被甲，兵象也。
於周易為離，離為戈兵。
」明年，瓘誅。
雞禍
魏明帝景初二年，廷尉府中有雌雞變為雄，不鳴不將。
干寶曰：「是歲，晉宣帝平遼東，百姓始有與能之議，此其象也。
」然晉三后並以人臣終，不鳴不將，又天意也。
晉惠帝元康六年，陳國有雞生雄雞無翅，既大，墜坑而死。
王隱曰：「雄，胤嗣象，坑地事為母象，賈后誣殺愍懷，殆其應也。」
晉惠帝太安中，周玘家有雌雞逃承霤中，六七日而下，奮翼鳴將，獨毛羽不變。
其後有陳敏之事。
敏雖控制江表，終無綱紀文章，殆其象也。
卒為玘所滅。
雞禍見玘家，又天意也。
晉元帝太興中，王敦鎮武昌，有雌雞化為雄。
天戒若曰：「雌化為雄，臣陵其上。
」其後王敦再攻京師。
晉孝武太元十三年四月，廣陵高平閻嵩家雄雞，生無右翅；
彭城到象之家雞，無右足。
京房易傳曰：「君用婦人言，則雞生妖。」
晉安帝隆安元年八月，琅邪王道子家青雌雞化為赤雄，不鳴不將。
後有桓玄之事，具如其象。
隆安四年，荊州有雞生角，角尋墮落。
是時桓玄始擅西夏，狂慢不肅，故有雞禍。
角，兵象；
尋墮落者，暫起不終之妖也。
晉安帝元興二年，衡陽有雌雞化為雄，八十日而冠萎。
衡陽，桓玄楚國封略也。
後篡位八十日而敗，徐廣以為玄之象也。
宋文帝元嘉十二年，華林園雌雞漸化為雄。
後孝武即位，皇太后令行于外，亦猶漢宣帝時，雌雞為雄，至哀帝時，元后與政也。
明帝泰始中，吳興東遷沈法符家雞有四距。
青眚青祥
晉武帝咸寧元年八月丁酉，大風折太社樹，有青氣出焉。
此青祥也。
占曰：「東莞當有帝者。
」明年，元帝生。
是時帝大父武王封東莞，由是徙封琅邪。
孫盛以為中興之表。
晉室之亂，武帝子孫無孑遺，社樹折之應，又恒風之罰也。
晉惠帝元康中，洛陽南山有䖟作聲曰：「韓屍屍。
」識者曰：「韓氏將死也。
言屍屍者，盡死意也。
」其後韓謐誅而韓族殲焉。
此青祥也。
金沴木
魏文帝初七年正月，幸許昌。
許昌城南門無故自崩，帝心惡之，遂不入，還洛陽。
此金沴木，木動也。
五月，宮車晏駕。
京房易傳曰：「上下咸悖，厥妖城門壞。」
晉元帝太興二年六月，吳郡米廩無故自壞。
是歲大饑，死者數千。
晉明帝太寧元年，周筵自歸王敦，既立宅宇，而所起五間六架，一時躍出墮地，餘桁猶亘柱頭。
此金沴木也。
明年五月，錢鳳謀亂，遂族滅筵，而湖熟尋亦為墟矣。
晉安帝元興元年正月丙子，司馬元顯將西討桓玄，建牙揚州南門，其東者難立，良久乃正。
近沴妖也。
尋為桓玄所禽。
元興三年五月，樂賢堂壞。
天意若曰，安帝嚚眊，不及有樂賢之心，故此堂見沴也。
晉安帝義熙九年五月乙酉，國子聖堂壞。
宋文帝元嘉十七年，劉斌為吳郡，郡堂屋西頭鴟尾無故落地，治之未畢，東頭鴟尾復落。
頃之，斌誅。
